headline: Why DIY Fire Cleanup Can Be a Huge Mistake
articleBody: When your home has been hit by fire, your first instinct might be to jump in and start cleaning up the mess yourself. It's totally understandable; you want your life back to normal as quickly as possible. But here's the thing: DIY fire cleanup often leads to bigger problems down the road. For one, soot and smoke residue aren't just ugly, they're acidic and can cause irreversible damage to surfaces if not cleaned properly and promptly. Also, the air quality after a fire is often compromised by microscopic particles that are harmful to breathe, even if they're not visible. Without the right protective gear and equipment, you could be risking your health. Another big one is water damage. Firefighting efforts often leave behind significant water damage, which, if not addressed immediately, can lead to mold growth and structural issues. And let's not forget about hidden damage; what looks fine to the untrained eye might be structurally compromised or have lingering smoke odors embedded deep within materials.
